verses.1: And the king sent for all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.2: And the king went into the Temple of God, along with all the Jews and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem. The priests, prophets, and all the people, from the smallest to the greatest, listened to all the words of the covenant that were written in the Temple of God.
verses.3: And the king stood on the throne, and he made a covenant before Jehovah. He vowed to follow Jehovah’s commands, keep His laws, and obey all His decrees with all his heart and soul. He wanted to fulfill the terms of this covenant, which were written on this scroll. And all the people stood together to make this covenant.
verses.4: The king commanded the high priest and the priests to bring out from the Temple of Jehovah all the utensils that were made for the Lord and for His people. They were then burned outside Jerusalem, in the courtyard of Kidron. The ashes were taken to the Temple.
verses.5: And he destroyed those instruments that were given by the kings of Judah. He also destroyed them in the cities of Judah and in Jerusalem. He also destroyed those instruments used for summoning the sun, the moon, and all the heavenly beings.
verses.6: And he took the remains out of the Temple of God, and carried them away to the valley of Kidron. There, he burned them in the valley of Kidron. Then he scattered the ashes over the bodies of the people.
verses.7: And he destroyed the holy houses that were in the house of God. The women who built those houses there were punished accordingly.
verses.8: And he brought all the priests from the cities of Judah. He cleaned out the altars that the priests had built on the hillsides from the Valley of Achor to Beer Sheba. He also destroyed the altars in the gates of Jerusalem, including the altar at the entrance of Jerusalem.
verses.9: But the priests of Baal shall not go to the altar of Yahweh in Jerusalem, unless they have eaten sacrifices within their own homes.
verses.10: And he covered the tomb where Ben-Hinnom’s son lay, so that no one could carry his son and daughter to the grave in flames.
verses.11: And he brought back the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, from the place where the Temple of God was located. He also brought back the chariots of the sun, which had been burned by fire.
verses.12: And the altars that were on the roof, which were made by the kings of Judah. And also the altars that Menashe built in the two courtyards of the Temple of God. The king was destroyed, and he ran away from there. He threw down their offerings into the river Kedron.
verses.13: And those gates that were on the walls of Jerusalem, on the right side of the Mount of Sorrows. Those gates were built by Solomon, king of Israel, for the purpose of protecting the people from harm. They served as a refuge for those who were in need, and also as a place where kings could suffer hardships at the hands of their own people.
verses.14: And he broke their positions, and he filled their places with human beings.
verses.15: And also, the altar that was in the house of God. It was made by Jeroboam, son of Nebat. He led Israel astray with this altar. He destroyed that altar as well. He burned down the altar completely.
verses.16: And Yosheiah saw the tombs that were there on the mountain. He then took the coffins from those tombs, burned them on the altar, and sealed them according to what the LORD had commanded. This was what the man of God said, who spoke these words.
verses.17: And he said, “What is this sign that I see?” And they said to him, “The people of the city say that there has come from Judah a man who is a god. He has done these things to the Temple of God.”
verses.18: And he said, “Let someone else take care of him; let him not try to move his own body.” Then his body was carried away by the prophet who came from Shomron.
verses.19: And also all the idols that were in the cities of Shimon, which were made by the kings of Israel to provoke God. Yosheiah was removed from those positions, and they were turned into objects like everything else that was made in the Temple.
verses.20: And he sacrificed all the priests who were there, on the altars. He also destroyed the images of men that were placed on those altars. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.21: And the king commanded all the people, “Let us celebrate Passover for the LORD your God, as it is written in the Book of the Covenant.”
verses.22: For this judgment was not made from the time of those who judged Israel, nor throughout all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
verses.23: For after eleven years of the king’s reign, this Passover was celebrated in Jerusalem.
verses.24: And also the scribes, the scholars, and all those who were skilled in writing. They were all found in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, in the area around Yerushalayim. This was done so that the words of the Torah could be written down on the scroll that the priest found.
verses.25: And as for him, there was no king like him before him who would return to Jehovah with all his heart, with all his soul, and with all his strength. No one like him has ever existed before or after him.
verses.26: But the LORD will not return that great punishment upon Judah, for He has punished them for all the troubles they caused to Manasseh.
verses.27: And the LORD said to Judah, “I will take away your glory from before My face, just as I took away the glory from Israel. I will also destroy this city that you have chosen for Jerusalem. And I will destroy the temple that I promised would be called My name.”
verses.28: And all the words of Josiah, and everything he did, are written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.29: In those days, Pharaoh Necho became king of Egypt. He attacked the king of Assyria along the river Euphrates. King Yosiah went to him to ask for help, but Pharaoh killed him in battle.
verses.30: His servants carried him away from his grave, and they brought him to Jerusalem. There, they buried him in his tomb. Then the people of the land took Yehohaz, son of Josiah, and sacrificed him. They made him king in place of his father.
verses.31: At the age of forty-three, he became king. For three years, he ruled in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal, daughter of Jirmeyahu from Bilbena.
verses.32: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his fathers had done.
verses.33: And Pharaoh Nekho forbade him to stay in Babylon, in the land of Hamath. He imposed a fine on that land: one hundred shekels of silver and one hundred shekels of gold.
verses.34: And Pharaoh ruled over Elyakim, son of Yosheiah. He took his name from Yosheiah, his father. He also took Yehoyakim’s wife and brought her into Egypt. There, Yehoyakim died.
verses.35: And the gold and silver were given to Pharaoh by Jehoiakim. But he valued the land more than the gold and silver. So he brought the gold and silver before Pharaoh, along with the people of that land.
verses.36: He reigned for forty-five years. He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Zebuda, daughter of Pedaya from Rumah.
verses.37: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his fathers had done.
